brief.headline: SK Hynix crosses $1T, HBM sold out 2026-27; DRAM Q2 +63% QoQ, NAND +75%; hyperscaler capex $700B
brief.summary: <cite index="6-1,6-22">SK Hynix's entire 2026 HBM allocation is sold out, with shortages projected into 2027.</cite> <cite index="38-1,38-2,38-10">SK Hynix surged 9.3% Wednesday, crossing $1 trillion market cap alongside Samsung Electronics at record 307,000 won, making South Korea the first nation outside the US with two trillion-dollar companies.</cite> <cite index="11-2,11-7">TrendForce forecasts Q2 2026 conventional DRAM contract prices rising 58-63% QoQ and NAND Flash 70-75% QoQ, following Q1's record 90-95% DRAM jump.</cite> <cite index="21-7,21-8">The four biggest hyperscalers will spend roughly $700 billion on capex in 2026, nearly double 2025 levels.</cite> <cite index="32-1,32-7">NVIDIA secured over 60% of TSMC's total CoWoS capacity for 2025-2026, while TSMC targets 120-130K wafers/month by end-2026, up from 75-80K currently.</cite>
brief.pair_trade_view: Long SK Hynix vs. Samsung. <cite index="39-4,39-8,39-9">SK Hynix market cap reached 93.2% of Samsung's (gap narrowed to 6.8%), with SK Hynix closing at record 2,289,000 won versus Samsung's 299,500 won.</cite> <cite index="43-11,43-12">SK Hynix Q1 revenue hit record ₩52.6T (+198% YoY), operating profit ₩37.61T (+405% YoY) with 72% margin, driven by heavy HBM3E/HBM4 focus.</cite> <cite index="5-5,5-27">UBS predicts SK Hynix will achieve approximately 70% market share in HBM4 for Nvidia's Rubin platform in 2026.</cite> <cite index="42-8">SK Hynix held 53% HBM market share Q3 2025 vs. Samsung's 35%.</cite> Purer HBM exposure, tighter execution, superior margins justify relative outperformance. Samsung's HBM4 qualification still unproven despite "customers say Samsung is back" rhetoric. SK Hynix 1Y +1,000%, Samsung +436%—momentum concentrated in memory pure-play.

memory_cycle.notes: <cite index="4-1">Goldman Sachs forecasting 4.9% DRAM supply deficit in 2026.</cite> <cite index="5-14">BofA forecasts global DRAM revenue +51% YoY, NAND +45% YoY, with ASPs rising 33% and 26% respectively.</cite> <cite index="14-8">Meaningful capacity expansion unlikely until late 2027 or 2028.</cite> <cite index="10-4,10-5">Producing 1 bit of HBM consumes ~300% the wafer capacity of 1 bit of DDR5; HBM has lower yields due to complex packaging.</cite> <cite index="10-9">AI will consume 20% of total DRAM production in 2026.</cite> Pricing power sustained through at least 2H 2026. Cyclicality debate ongoing—structurally higher baseline vs. traditional boom-bust.

brief.hbm_pulse: <cite index="5-18">BofA estimates 2026 HBM market to reach $54.6B (+58% YoY).</cite> <cite index="5-19,5-20">Goldman Sachs forecasts HBM demand for custom ASIC-based AI chips will skyrocket 82%, accounting for one-third of the market, indicating diversification beyond general-purpose GPUs.</cite> <cite index="5-21,5-22">HBM3E remains flagship product in 2026, with Nvidia Blackwell Ultra, Google, and AWS expanding proprietary ASIC chips selecting HBM3E.</cite> <cite index="2-11,2-13">SK Hynix announced iHBM thermal architecture integrating cooling elements inside HBM interface, cutting thermal resistance by 30%, targeting next-gen HBM5 accelerators.</cite> <cite index="3-4,3-5,3-6">Korean memory manufacturer discussing separating GPUs and HBM into separate packages connected via optical links, potentially allowing several times more HBM than existing designs.</cite> Technology roadmap advancing ahead of supply.

news_pulse.headline: SK Hynix crosses $1T market cap, KOSPI hits all-time high 8,457
news_pulse.implication: Validates HBM scarcity narrative. SK Hynix now #12 globally, Samsung #11. KOSPI concentration risk—two names >40% of index. Forced fund selling $69B (Goldman) despite bullish fundamentals. Proxy plays (SK Square +1,000% 1Y, Samsung Life 3x) signal indirect exposure demand.

news_pulse.headline: TrendForce upgrades Q2 2026 DRAM to +58-63% QoQ, NAND +70-75%
news_pulse.implication: Sequential pricing acceleration continues but DRAM QoQ growth decelerating from Q1's 90-95%. NAND outpacing DRAM for first time this cycle—enterprise SSD absorption intensifying. Client SSD/PC DRAM lowest priority; consumer downgrades spreading.

news_pulse.headline: Hyperscalers commit $700B capex 2026, up ~2x from 2025
news_pulse.implication: Microsoft $120B+, Alphabet $175-185B, Amazon $200B, Meta $125-145B, Oracle $50B. Two-thirds of MSFT capex = short-lived assets (GPUs/CPUs, 3-5Y depreciation). Meta cited "higher component pricing" in raise. Demand signal unambiguous; memory/HBM allocation politics intensifying.

news_pulse.headline: TSMC CoWoS capacity targeting 120-130K wpm by end-2026, up from 75-80K
news_pulse.implication: NVIDIA locked 60%+ of 2025-26 allocation. TSMC outsourcing 240-270K wafers/year to Amkor (180-190K) and SPIL (60-80K) for margin optimization. CoWoS-L demand (RDL interposers) redirecting internal capacity. CoPoS mass production late 2027—transition risk for round-wafer lines.

news_pulse.headline: SK Hynix-Intel testing 2.5D EMIB for HBM integration amid CoWoS shortage
news_pulse.implication: Diversification of advanced packaging supply chain. Intel EMIB-T w/ TSVs targeting HBM4/4e (32Gbps+ per pin). SK Hynix hedging TSMC dependency—aligns with memory-centric vertical integration strategy.

news_pulse.headline: BofA names SK Hynix "Top Pick," forecasts DRAM revenue +51% YoY, NAND +45%
news_pulse.implication: "Supercycle similar to 1990s boom." ASP gains (DRAM +33%, NAND +26%) driving profitability. Reinforces SK Hynix as primary anchor of AI memory shift. HBM3E→HBM4 dual-generation support differentiates vs. Samsung.

news_pulse.headline: Memory shortage debate: structural vs. cyclical risks resurface
news_pulse.implication: Deutsche Bank cites TurboQuant AI inference efficiency as potential demand disruptor (structural shift "remains to be seen"). JM Finn: production could increase meaningfully next 3Y if AI demand normalizes. Valuation assumes prolonged pricing discipline and high margins—cyclical tail risk non-zero.

news_pulse.headline: Samsung-SK Hynix gap narrows to 6.8%; SK Hynix at 93.2% of Samsung market cap
news_pulse.implication: Simulation using brokerage high targets (Samsung ₩570K, SK Hynix ₩3.8M) yields SK Hynix 81.3% of Samsung—suggests Samsung won't easily cede #1 spot. But momentum favors SK Hynix near-term on purer memory exposure.

brief.derivatives_signal: Elevated vol environment; forced rebalancing flows creating technical volatility despite fundamental strength. New leveraged ETFs on Samsung/SK Hynix launched—retail momentum chase. Proxy derivatives (SK Square, Samsung Life) trading >10x leverage to underlying due to concentration limits. Watch for gamma unwind if KOSPI breaches index concentration thresholds. Options skew likely favoring upside (supply scarcity narrative intact) but tail hedge demand rising on cyclical/valuation concerns.
watch_for_next_3h: KOSPI concentration rule enforcement—mechanical selling if Samsung+SK Hynix >43-45% threshold breached
Any Samsung HBM4 qualification/Nvidia certification news (would tighten pair spread)

TSMC CoWoS June allocation updates or yield disclosures (Blackwell/Rubin ramp)
